title: Today in one sentence
text: The market closed mixed on Thursday: the S&P 500 fund SPY rose 0.3% and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ slipped 0.1%, while chip stocks fell even after TSMC reported better than expected results; tomorrow, watch whether chips keep sliding or bounce back.

title: Chip stocks dipped despite good news
text: TSMC reported earnings per share of $4.60 against the $4.45 analysts expected, and sales of about $46.5 billion, also above forecasts. Yet TSMC fell 1.8%, NVIDIA 1.8%, AMD 1.5% and Vertiv 3.6%. Sometimes a stock drops on good news because investors had already hoped for even more. That is why prices can fall when a company does well.

title: Big companies beat chip suppliers today
text: Microsoft rose 1.1%, Alphabet 0.5% and Amazon 0.3%, while all five AI supplier stocks on the list closed lower. Companies that build AI chips and equipment tend to swing more than the big companies that buy them, so they move up and down by larger amounts.

title: Rocket Lab dropped 6.6%
text: Rocket Lab is a stock with a very high beta of 2.6, meaning it tends to move much more than the market. It is now about 63% below its 52 week high, which is why our risk score for it is the highest on the board. A stock that fell a lot is not automatically a bargain; it can mean the market sees more risk.

title: Earnings week ahead for three names
text: An earnings report is a company's report card for the last three months. According to market calendars, GE Aerospace is expected to report on Oct. 20, Meta on Oct. 21 and Lockheed Martin on Oct. 22. Prices often jump around these dates, so expect bigger moves than usual.

title: Lesson 9: ETFs vs single stocks
text: A single stock is a tiny piece of one company. An ETF (exchange traded fund) is a basket that holds pieces of many companies, and you buy the whole basket in one step. Look at today. NVIDIA, a single stock, fell 1.8%. The SPY fund, which holds 500 big US companies, rose 0.3%. The basket was calmer because the winners and losers in it partly cancel each other out. That is diversification, which Lesson 4 explained, built into one purchase. The tradeoff: a single stock can grow much faster than a basket if the company does great, but it can also fall much harder if the company stumbles. A basket will never be the top performer, and it will rarely be the worst. Many investors keep a basket as the base and add a few single stocks around it only if they understand each company.

title: What this covers
text: Prices are from Thursday's close. Analyst price targets and company numbers are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, GE Aerospace and Lockheed Martin. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have prices and risk scores only. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell anything.
